title: Debug: Part 2
summary: Trace aliases, numeric **edges**, mutation, and boundaries.
refresher: Harder Java bugs can originate in shared **object** references, **integer** arithmetic, or an **edge case** skipped by normal input. Record state just before and after its first incorrect change.

sections.title: Check whether two variables share one object
sections.summary: **Array** and object **variables** can point at the same mutable data.

blocks.body: In Java, an **array** **variable** stores a reference to an array **object**. Assigning one array variable to another copies the reference, not the elements. If both variables point at one array, changing an element through either variable changes the same array.

blocks.title: Find the first wrong state
blocks.caption: Compare expected and actual state until the first wrong transition is isolated.

blocks.caption: The first version prints `9` because both **variables** reach the same **array**. The cloned version prints `1`.
The equality check here asks whether the two **variables** point at the exact same **array** **object**.

choices: every element into a new array
blocks.why: Both **variables** point to one **array** **object** until code explicitly clones or copies the elements.

sections.title: Inspect numeric and boundary assumptions
sections.summary: **Integer division** and empty arrays can make correct-looking code return the wrong answer.

blocks.body: A Java program can compile and still lose information. If both operands are **integers**, division happens as **integer division** before the result is stored. Boundary inputs need the same attention: an empty **array** has no first or last element to inspect.

blocks.caption: The cast must happen before division. Otherwise `7 / 2` becomes `3`, and then Java stores `3.0` in the double.

blocks.prompt: Why can an average lose its decimal?
blocks.why: When both operands are **integers**, Java performs **integer division** before assigning the result.

sections.title: Check null and range before access
sections.summary: Many runtime bugs happen one line before the value is used.

blocks.body: Before reading from an array, list, or object, check whether the reference exists and whether the index is in range. The safest debug trace names the value you are about to access.

blocks.caption: Guard the access before it happens.

blocks.prompt: What should be checked before reading `values[0]`?
choices: that the array has at least one item
blocks.why: Index 0 is valid only when the array length is at least one.

sections.title: Choose copy, mutate, or build new data
sections.summary: Collection bugs get easier once you decide whether the original object should change.

blocks.body: If a method should leave the input alone, avoid changing the original array or list. Make a copy or write into a new result structure.

blocks.caption: Removing while scanning can skip nearby values because later items shift left.

blocks.prompt: Why can a new list be safer than removing while scanning?
choices: Indexes do not shift under the loop
It turns the list into an array
blocks.why: The original scan order stays stable when kept values are written into a separate list.

debug-p2-01.title: Empty input changes the math
debug-p2-01.body: A formula that works for normal data can fail when the collection has no items.
debug-p2-01.notice: Check the divisor or first access before running the normal-case calculation.
debug-p2-01.mistake: Do not divide by a count before checking whether the count is zero.

debug-p2-02.title: Reset per-row state inside the outer loop
debug-p2-02.body: State for one row should restart before scanning that row.
debug-p2-02.notice: Ask whether the variable belongs to the whole grid or only the current row.
debug-p2-02.mistake: Do not let a previous row leak into the next row's total.

debug-p2-03.title: Binary search moves toward the possible half
debug-p2-03.body: When the middle value is too small, the target must be to the right in sorted data.
debug-p2-03.notice: Move the lower bound past mid when mid is too small.
debug-p2-03.mistake: Do not move a boundary backward into the half you already ruled out.

debug-p2-04.title: Removal shifts later items
debug-p2-04.body: Removing the current item moves the next item into the same index.
debug-p2-04.notice: After removal, either recheck the current index, move backward, or build a filtered result.
debug-p2-04.mistake: Do not increment blindly after a removal if adjacent items may also need removal.

debug-p2-05.title: Initial best must come from possible data
debug-p2-05.body: A starting best value that is not in the input can beat every real value by accident.
debug-p2-05.notice: For maximum or minimum, initialize from the first item when possible.
debug-p2-05.mistake: Do not use zero as a default when all real values might be below zero.

debug-p2-06.title: Second place may need distinctness
debug-p2-06.body: Tracking largest and second largest requires a rule for duplicates.
debug-p2-06.notice: Decide whether equal-to-largest values are allowed before updating second.
debug-p2-06.mistake: Do not let the same value occupy both largest and second when the prompt asks for distinct values.

debug-p2-07.title: Do not count the first value twice
debug-p2-07.body: Preloading a running total and then looping over every item can add the first item again.
debug-p2-07.notice: Choose either start at zero and loop all items, or start at first and loop the rest.
debug-p2-07.mistake: Do not combine both patterns unless the prompt needs double counting.

debug-p2-08.title: Mirror checks need opposite sides
debug-p2-08.body: A palindrome-style comparison pairs the left position with the matching right position.
debug-p2-08.notice: Compute the right index from the length and the left index.
debug-p2-08.mistake: Do not compare neighboring characters when the prompt asks for mirrored characters.
